note: Tracker update scheduling. Runs are 2 minutes apart (dispatched by the Cloudflare Worker in worker/, not by the cron in tracker.yml) and RUN_SPACING_MS matches. A player is scraped when its interval has elapsed AND its slot matches the run, where slots = round(interval / RUN_SPACING_MS). The 0.025h (90s) interval below is deliberately SHORTER than the 120s spacing: that gives 1 slot, so every player is due on every run, and it leaves margin for dispatch jitter (at exactly 120s a run arriving a second early skips the whole roster and doubles the gap). Measured cost: ~0.55s per player at 60 players, in a ~65s run. intervalMultiplier multiplies EVERY interval - keep it at 1 unless deliberately throttling. perRun is a CEILING on how many players one run may scrape, not a target: with fewer players than the ceiling every due player still runs. Raised 110 -> 150 on 10 September 2026 because the roster had reached 104 and left only six of headroom. Past the ceiling the scheduler silently defers the overflow, which looks like a stalled collector rather than a config limit, and nothing warns about it. Bandwidth is not the reason to keep it low: measured that day, the whole fleet ran at 4.4% of its 500 GB allowance, about 0.21 GB per player per month. The real limit is run WALL-CLOCK, and it is already binding. MEASURED 10 September 2026 over 12 consecutive runs at 104 players: 144-175s, median 162s end to end (checkout, install and browser launch included), so ~1.56s per player rather than the 0.55s measured at 60. Runs are dispatched every 120s but take longer than that, and `concurrency: cancel-in-progress: false` in tracker.yml makes them QUEUE rather than cancel - GitHub keeps only one pending run, so a newer dispatch replaces the waiting one. The effective scrape interval is therefore the RUN DURATION (~162s), not the 120s dispatch cadence, and some dispatches are harmlessly discarded. Data is consequently ~3 minutes old at best, not 2; the liveness alarm at 10 minutes is unaffected. At 150 players a run would be around 4 minutes. Measure `gh run list --workflow=tracker.yml` before raising the ceiling again, and treat run duration as the number that actually limits the roster. idleMultiplier stretches the interval for a player Steam reports as NOT in Rocket League, so an idle pro is re-read every ~15 minutes instead of every run. They cannot be gaining MMR or games while out of the game, and matchesPlayed is cumulative, so nothing is lost - only the 24h window edge and how fast the Playing pill lights up soften. It applies ONLY to an explicit "out" from presenceHot; a private or hidden-details profile reports "unknown" and keeps full cadence, which is about half the roster. Set to 1 to disable. Added 10 September 2026 because tracker.gg rate-limits per IP and the fleet had reached 89% failure with 14 of 15 proxies refused: cutting requests per IP is the fix that does not expire, unlike replacing addresses. MEASURED 10 September 2026 against the live roster of 106: at a busy hour 54 scrapes per run instead of 106 (49% fewer). Modelled across a day using the owner's own observation of how many pros play at once - peak 15, typical 7, roughly none overnight - it gives 39 / 32 / 26 scrapes per run, which is 63% / 70% / 76% fewer, and takes per-IP load from 262 requests an hour to 97 / 80 / 64 at nine working proxies. Note Steam's "in" means in the APP, not in a ranked match: about twice as many report in-game as show the Playing pill, because menus, freeplay, training and casual all count. Gating is deliberately conservative for that reason - somebody sitting in a menu keeps full cadence because they can queue at any moment.
